text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended with pared gains on Friday after the arabica futures on the New York market turned sluggish and prices drifted lower on light selling. September was actively traded and ended the day $11 higher at $1,590 a tonne, after the day's high of $1,617. November was just $10 up at $1,580.

Arabica futures finished broadly lower in dull trade, pressured by light commission house selling, floor sources said. Benchmark September ended down 4.10 cents at 176.30 cents/lb, after ranging from 182.00 to 175.50 cents. Second month December ended 3.05 cents lower at 157.25 cents/lb, while the back months shed 0.95 to 3.45 cents.

The September/December switch narrowed to 19.05 cents/lb, down from 20.10 cents at the close the previous day. Concern about deliverable supplies against the September contract are likely to keep the September at a strong premium to the December. Technically, traders said September's support was seen near 174.25 cents/lb while resistance was pegged at 184.50 cents/lb.

UNITED STATES - CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 2,183 60-kg bags as of July 24, to 92,828 bags. An additional 3,738 bags were pending grading, the Exchange said. According to trade sources, some of the African coffee that passed the CSCE's grading system for July delivery was not good enough according to the industry's quality standards.

Of the supply available for July delivery the majority came from Burundi and Uganda. One trade house was rumoured to have appealed its delivery notices after stopping poor quality coffee which was thought to be of African origin.

UNITED STATES - For the week ended July 19, roastings totalled approximately 320,000 60-kg bags, up from 285,000 bags the previous week and compared with 350,000 bags in the corresponding period one year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage reported. Cumulative roastings so far totalled 9.435 million 60-kg bags vs 9.220 million bags in the same year-ago period.

FINLAND - Coffee imports in April 1997 amounted to 122,200 bags, which brought cumulative imports in the first four months of 1997 (January/April) up to 422,300 bags, up almost 35 per cent on the tonnage imported in the corresponding period the previous year. Total imports in 1996 amounted to 1.120 million bags compared to 758,500 bags in 1995. Major suppliers of green coffee in 1997 were Brazil (107,400 vs 48,300 bags), Colombia (87,000 vs 92,600 bags) and Costa Rica (54,100 vs 27,900 bags).

Coffee exports in January/April 1997 reached 68,400 bags compared to 44,200 bags in 1996. Total exports in 1996 were 172,500 bags vs 96,800 bags in 1995. The major country of destination in 1997 was Sweden which took 37,600 bags of roast and ground compared to 24,500 bags in 1996.

BRAZIL - Brazil's coffee crop in 1997 should reach 2.46 million tonnes in cherry, down 3.22 per cent from a forecast of 2.55 million tonnes issued at the end of June, the National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said. The drop is due to an adjustment in production forecasts from Minas Gerais state, the IBGE said.

The most recent estimate also marks a 6.42 per cent fall from the 2.64 million tonnes produced last year. The IBGE figures are in cherry whereas other forecasts are normally in green coffee beans. Agronomists say there is no reliable formula to convert cherry estimates to beans.
